title: Teen Reset Pack
description: For parents supporting teens experiencing low energy, sadness, or withdrawal. These micro-routines encourage structure, connection, and gentle activation.

routines.title: Share the Morning Light
routines.description: Start the day together by opening the curtains or stepping outside for 2 minutes.
routines.parentGoal: Help reset circadian rhythm and create gentle activation.
steps: Invite your teen to open the curtains or step outside with you.
Say something simple like, 'Let’s get some light together.'
Notice one thing in nature aloud ('the sky looks clear today').

routines.title: Tiny Move Together
routines.parentGoal: Support physical activation and lower emotional inertia.
routines.childOutcome: Increased energy and dopamine boost through movement.
steps: Say, 'Let’s do three minutes of something active together.'
Offer options: stretch, walk around the block, or dance to a song.
Keep it playful—no performance or pressure.

routines.title: Soft Check-In
routines.description: A low-pressure moment to connect with your teen through a brief text or comment.
routines.parentGoal: Maintain gentle connection even when talking feels hard.
steps: Send a short message like, 'Thinking of you—want a snack?'
Or make a light comment in person, not a question ('That sunset’s wild tonight.').
Leave space; no need for a reply.

routines.title: Five-Minute Evening Walk
routines.description: Invite your teen for a no-talking walk around the block or house.
routines.parentGoal: Provide sensory calm and subtle presence.
routines.childOutcome: Lower stress hormones; emotional regulation through rhythm and movement.
steps: Say, 'I need a little air, want to come?'
Keep your phone away; silence is okay.

routines.title: Model Self-Kindness
routines.description: Show your teen how you write or say one kind thing to yourself.
routines.parentGoal: Model self-compassion as a coping skill.
steps: Write a short note to yourself on a sticky note ('I’m doing my best today.').
Place it on the mirror where your teen can see.
If they notice, invite them to write one too.
